title: Autoscale threshold ladder experiments and oscillation mitigation (Oct 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

We ran a set of targeted autoscaler experiments ("threshold ladder") across three regions to evaluate whether graduated scale triggers + step-scaling + dynamic cooldown reduces flapping/oscillation under bursty request patterns for high-memory GPU clusters (A100/80GB equivalent pools). Results show a 65–83% reduction in oscillation events, a median latency SLO improvement of 12–23% during bursts, and a modest 4–7% cost increase in worst-case steady-state compared with the aggressive min/max policy currently in prod.

Objective:
- Reduce frequent scale-up/scale-down oscillations caused by short bursts and erratic usage while preserving latency SLOs (p95 < 200ms per-token on streaming workloads).
- Keep committed capacity predictable for billing, avoid unnecessary GPU spin-ups during short noise bursts.
- Identify a simple, region-safe policy template to pilot to Dedicated customers.

Experiment design summary:
- Approach: implement a "threshold ladder" where scale-up/down decisions are tiered (soft->firm->critical) with increasing aggressiveness and longer cooldowns at higher tiers. Step-scaling: scale by N nodes depending on the active tier rather than full jump to max or single-node increments.
- Workloads simulated: synthetic chat bursts (90s bursts with exponential interarrival tail), embedding batch spikes (2–5k concurrent short jobs), and mixed steady+burst traffic (traffic shadowing from prod traces).
- Regions: us-west1, eu-central1, ap-southeast1.
- Hardware: GPU pool types representative of Dedicated (A100-80 equivalent).

Key variables tested:
- min_nodes / max_nodes (range tested 2–48 per pool)
- scale_up_trigger: CPU/GPU utilization thresholds, queue length, token-rate windows (10s, 30s, 60s)
- scale_down_trigger: similar metrics with separate thresholds and cooldown multipliers
- cooldown_s: varied 30s -> 1800s depending on tier
- step_size: 1, 2, 4, 8 nodes depending on tier and region

Representative config patterns (notation: tier(name) = (trigger, cooldown_s, step)):
- baseline-aggressive = (util>=65% over 30s, cooldown 120s, step=4)  // current-ish prod policy we use for new clusters
- ladder-soft = (util>=50% over 60s, cooldown 180s, step=1)
- ladder-firm = (util>=70% over 30s, cooldown 300s, step=2)
- ladder-critical = (util>=85% over 10s, cooldown 900s, step=4)

Experiment matrix (summary table):

ID | region | min/max | policy | avg_osc_per_hour | p95_latency_delta | cost_delta | dropped_jobs | notes
E1 | us-west1 | 4/32 | baseline-aggressive | 7.8 | +0% | baseline | 3 | frequent oscillation during tail bursts
E2 | us-west1 | 4/32 | threshold-ladder (soft->firm->critical) | 1.2 | -18% | +5% | 0 | best tradeoff for this region
E3 | eu-central1 | 2/24 | ladder + step-size adaptive | 0.9 | -12% | +4% | 0 | slightly higher cold-starts on scale-up but steady latency
E4 | ap-southeast1 | 6/48 | ladder + longer cooldowns | 2.6 | -10% | +7% | 1 | noisy burst pattern caused one transient drop; use higher step for region
E5 | us-west1 | 2/8 | ladder-soft + small max | 0.5 | -23% | -2% | 0 | when capacity headroom small, ladder avoids overprovisioning but increases p90 cold-start tail initially

Raw metric highlights (selected):
- E2 (us-west1): oscillation events reduced from 76 events/day -> 11 events/day across test window. Median time between oscillations increased from 12m -> 128m.
- E3 (eu-central1): average node churn decreased by 63%; tail token latency p99 reduced by 34% during bursts.
- E4 (ap-southeast1): cost delta +7% driven by larger min_nodes chosen for region-specific availability; but user-observed p95 improved by 14%.

Notable failure modes observed:
1) Rapid small bursts shorter than the shortest trigger window (10s) still caused micro-up/down cycles on pools with min_nodes <=2. Mitigation: enforce a soft minimum of 3 nodes for any production pool handling streaming chat.
2) Queue-length-only triggers misfired during bulk-embedding jobs where queue drains fast but GPU utilization remains high; combining queue-length + token-rate window improved signal quality.
3) Region-specific provisioning lag: ap-southeast observed longer VM/GPU provisioning times; longer scale-up step sizes reduced the number of provisioning waves and smoothed latency but increased cost.

Operational recommendations (pilot):
- Adopt ladder template as default for new Dedicated pools: soft(60s, step=1) -> firm(30s, step=2) -> critical(10s, step=4) with cooldown multipliers [1x, 2x, 6x] respectively.
- Minimum node floor: set min_nodes >= 3 for streaming-chat-critical pools; consider min_nodes >=6 for APAC pools with known provisioning lag.
- Signal composition: require at least two of {GPU_util_window, token_rate_window, queue_length_trend} to be above thresholds to trigger up/downs (reduce single-signal noise).
- Step-sizing: prefer step sizes that approximate 20–30% of current pool size (rounded) when above firm tier to avoid many small provisioning operations.
- Monitoring: add "oscillation-rate" as an SLI (events/hour where up and down happened within 15m) and alert at >5 events/hour per pool.

Suggested rollout plan:
1) Canary in us-west1 on three low-risk customers (2–3 pools) for 2 weeks; collect SLI data and user-facing latency traces.
2) Expand to eu-central1 with adjusted min_nodes and step-sizing after 1 week evaluation.
3) For APAC, run extended soak (4 weeks) due to provisioning variability and region-specific cost delta.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we expose an autoscaler policy preview API to estimate cost delta for customer-proposed min/max before committing? (Product/console ask)
- Should Dedicated offer a "latency-first" preset vs "cost-first" preset using these ladder defaults? (GTM ask)
- Need a small RFC on storing per-pool provisioning latency quantiles so the autoscaler can pick region-aware cooldown/step sizes automatically.

Appendix A: Full per-experiment numeric dump (selected fields)
- E2_us-west1_ladder: total_scale_ups=18, total_scale_downs=9, mean_cooldown=312s, avg_nodes_during_peak=21.4, median_boot_time=92s, osc_events=11
- E3_eu-central1_adaptive: total_scale_ups=12, total_scale_downs=4, mean_cooldown=280s, avg_nodes_during_peak=16.1, median_boot_time=84s, osc_events=8

Appendix B: Quick checklist for SEs when proposing Dedicated pool config to customers
- Confirm expected burst profile (duration, frequency)
- Recommend min_nodes >= 3 for streaming workloads
- Choose ladder preset (latency-first vs cost-first) and annotate expected cost delta
- Run 72-hour shadow test with ladder policy before final commit

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Convert the most relevant experiment data into a short deck for PS and Sales by 2026-10-25. Maya to take first draft.
- Open Jira tasks to instrument "oscillation-rate" and add an SLI dashboard. Assigned: Ben.
- Explore a small ML classifier to predict provisioning lag per region based on historical boot times (R&D spike).

End of sheet.
